summary:
We built a web dashboard that turns NASA's microgravity combustion data into fire safety answers. From 24 investigations in the PSI database, we assembled a unified dataset of 1,200 real tests from 9 experiments and trained predictive models on it. The user sets a cabin atmosphere (oxygen, pressure) and gets a prediction: the chance that a gas-leak flame self-extinguishes, or how long a fuel droplet burns. For solid materials, where the data cannot support a model, it shows the closest real tests instead.

It addresses the challenge in three ways: it profiles and ranks the investigations by relevance to each crewed habitat (spacecraft, station, lunar base, Martian base, rover), it extracts data that supports predictive modeling, and it lists findings that inform fire safety equipment. An AI assistant and an open API sit on top.

It matters because the planned Moon Base will run at 30% oxygen or more, where materials burn far more easily. Every prediction shows its error margin and was validated on tests the model had never seen (84% accuracy on gas leaks).
details:
WHAT IT DOES

The dashboard has four tabs. Simulator: the user sets a cabin atmosphere (oxygen, pressure, diluents) and a fire type, and gets a prediction. For a gas leak, the probability that the flame self-extinguishes; for a fuel droplet, the time until it goes out; for solid materials, the closest real tests, since the data cannot support a model there. Investigations: profiles of all 24 PSI combustion investigations, comparable side by side. Environments: a relevance ranking for spacecraft, space station, lunar base, Martian base and pressurized rover. Equipment: findings for detectors, suppression, ventilation and materials, each tagged as measured, model or report. An AI assistant answers questions by calling the same models, so it cannot invent numbers.

HOW IT WORKS

We consolidated the raw PSI files into one dataset of 1,200 tests from 9 experiments. The gas-leak model is a logistic regression trained on the BRE experiment; the droplet model is a gradient-boosted survival model (XGBoost AFT), which handles tests that ended before the flame went out. Both were validated on test days the model had never seen. The trained trees were exported to JSON and run in JavaScript, so predictions happen in the browser and match the Python version.

BENEFITS AND IMPACT

Engineers and researchers get an answer in seconds instead of digging through 14 GB of files. Every prediction shows its error margin, the real tests behind it, and a warning when it extrapolates. This matters for the planned Moon Base atmosphere of 30% oxygen or more.

TOOLS

Python, DuckDB, XGBoost, FastAPI, JavaScript, Cloudflare Workers, Claude Code, and a language model for the assistant and for labeling test outcomes. Data and API are open.

CREATIVITY AND FACTORS CONSIDERED

The dashboard states what it does not know: no partial-gravity data exists in PSI, so lunar and Martian results are bounded by microgravity and 1 g; the dataset is small, so models are simple; and it is not a substitute for NASA's standard flammability tests.
